dialogue.content: I-I wasn't going to volunteer! I was simply... assessing the threat profile! A crusader must know her enemies! The grappling and dragging is entirely incidental to my tactical analysis! (Her voice rises an octave with each sentence, face now fully crimson.)

For your information, Kazuma, my dawn Explosion was flawlessly executed. The shockwave alone cleared three blocks of pigeons. To call that a 'daily budget' is to reduce art to accounting — a crime for which there is no forgiveness in any legal system, Crimson Demon or otherwise. (She brandishes the napkin like a courtroom exhibit, then wobbles and grabs the table edge.)

Hey! You were about to say something to me and then you just walked away! Were you going to tell me to stop drinking? Because that would be discrimination against the divine! I'll have you know this is ceremonial — it's a purification ritual! (She points at you with theatrical accusation.)
Good morning. I see your party is... as energetic as ever. (Her smile remains perfectly, terrifyingly serene.)

I have not asked about a crater, a fountain, or a missing statue. Though I appreciate — genuinely — your proactive disclosure policy. (Her smile remains fixed, but one eyebrow lifts a fraction of an inch as she sets the scroll on the counter between them.)

This is a Brutal Alligator subjugation request. The sewers beneath the commercial district. They've been breeding. The reward is forty thousand eris. I am sorry. (She slides the scroll forward with two fingers, the gesture of a woman who has handed doomed adventurers their last quest before.)

You are, of course, correct. A divine drinking challenge, a grappling-based religious experience, and I suspect Miss Megumin would find some way to make the sewer ceiling open to the sky. (her smile tightens by that same one millimeter, but her voice stays warm)

I am very sorry. That is not a joke. The reward is forty thousand eris, your party's tab is currently... substantial... and you are the only adventurers in Axel who haven't already refused this quest. (slides the scroll across the counter toward you with both hands, like she's offering a sacred relic she personally finds terrifying)
They want the nest gone entirely. Every last egg. The merchants were very specific about the eggs. (taps the supplementary document with her fingernail, then folds her hands back atop the counter)

The sewer maintenance office keeps this schematic current — mostly. The main drainage artery runs east-west beneath the commercial district. The eastern outflow gate is where the shipments are blocked. That's where the last two parties entered. They didn't come back, so I can't tell you how many alligators are down there. Merchant reports mention at least three adults, but those reports are three weeks old and alligators breed. (traces the schematic with a steady finger, tapping junctions as she names them)

The merchant guild is offering forty thousand eris for full extermination — nest, eggs, everything. Their addendum is very specific about the eggs. Every single one destroyed. They added ten thousand to the hazard fee just to make that binding. (folds her hands atop the documents, meeting the Player's eyes with a steady, apologetic smile)

An edge?! My sacred purification magic is not an 'edge,' Kazuma — it's a divine instrument of absolute, cataclysmic annihilation! But I suppose even a goddess of my stature can lower herself to frontline duty. For now. As a favor. (Snatches her tankard back up for a victory sip, misses her mouth slightly, does not notice.)

And the second group — you said two groups — that would be Megumin and myself, yes? Holding the rear junction, drawing the flanking assault, every fang and every claw converging while I stand alone in the dark with only my armor and my fa— (Her voice climbs in both pitch and temperature; she is half out of her chair, and the table leg beneath her grip has developed a visible crack.)

Do not volunteer me for sewer-rearguard duty, Darkness. I have already delivered my Explosion to the dawn. My mana is not merely depleted — it is transcendentally exhausted. I am present in a strictly consultative capacity. (Does not open her other eye. Her voice is flat, freighted with the particular dignity of someone who cannot currently feel her legs.)

Thirty to fifty alligators, six weeks from hatch to full maturity, all of them directly under the commercial district's foundations. A single survivor could restart the nest. That is why the bonus exists — ten thousand eris is cheaper than evacuating half the district when the tunnel ceilings start collapsing under the weight of a breeding colony. (Luna taps the sub-clause with her fingernail, then slides the document toward you so the fine print is legible.)

Heads, tails, or any portion large enough that no one can argue the creature is still breathing. The eggs, however, must be destroyed on-site — the addendum is explicit. Crushed, burned, dissolved. No removal, no sale. The merchants added that clause after the last party tried to smuggle a clutch to a breeder in Elroad. (Her tone on the last sentence is flat — not judgment, exactly, but the weariness of a woman who has had to add too many sub-clauses to too many quests because of too many enterprising adventurers.)

Three ales?! I'll have you know my tolerance is divine! A goddess doesn't get 'three ales in' — she gets ceremonially purified! And if anything, the ale sharpens my holy senses! (Slams her tankard again, then realizes it's empty and looks tragically into its depths.)

An archwizard who can't cast? Kazuma, you wound me with the precision of a man who has forgotten that Explosion is not merely a spell — it is a covenant! True, my mana lies dormant until dawn, but my tactical genius remains fully operational! I can still point dramatically at things! (Attempts to cross her arms, misses the first attempt, succeeds on the second with considerable focus.)

Y-you were about to say 'provoke,' weren't you? A crusader who'll provoke every monster in the sewer... You think I'd throw myself into danger and jeopardize the mission. Perhaps you're right — perhaps my very presence is a liability, and you should reconsider bringing me at all... (Voice drops to a breathless murmur; she is visibly disappointed when she realizes she's arguing herself out of the quest and quickly course-corrects.)

But as a Crusader of the Dustiness house, I swear I shall exercise restraint! Every alligator that bites me will be one that isn't biting you — that's simple arithmetic! (Slams her own gauntlet on the table, rattling the schematic, then realizes she's drawn attention and goes crimson.)

The quest is registered to your party. I'll mark it as accepted pending execution — you have seventy-two hours before the guild must re-post. The merchants won't like the delay, but the merchants aren't the ones going into the sewer. (Pen scratches once across the ledger. The receptionist-smile returns, but it's the smaller, realer one — the one that means she's not required to pretend.)

The guild kitchen keeps two. The large one is copper — heats fast, but the handle's loose. The small one is iron and older than I am, but it'll boil steady and it won't tip when she flails. (She is already reaching beneath the counter for a key, her tone matter-of-fact, as though she has been asked to sober up adventurers often enough to have a preferred kettle for the job.)

Kazuma. Kazuma, you can't be serious. That's — that's alcohol abuse! Pouring cold water on a goddess is a Class-A celestial insult! I'll have you reported to the Axis Order tribunal! (She clutches her tankard to her chest like a shield, scooting her stool back two inches.)

A goddess felled not by demon king nor undead horde, but by the humble kettle. Truly, the Crimson Demon archives will record this as the most pathetic defeat in Axis history. Do proceed. (She does not open her other eye, but the corner of her mouth twitches upward.)

I cannot amend the merchant guild's contract. But I can note on the quest record that the party leader retains retreat authority pending an on-site assessment. If you return with evidence the nest exceeds the original scouting report, that addendum gives the guild grounds to open re-negotiation. (slides the blank addendum form toward the Player, her fingertip resting on the signature line)
A contingency clause. Luna, you are nearly as cunning as a Crimson Demon. (lifts her chin from her staff, a flicker of genuine respect crossing her exhausted features)

Wait — you're just going to let him write his own exit clause? He's not even an advanced class! I'm a goddess and I don't get custom paperwork! (gestures wildly at the addendum, nearly knocking over her tankard, then freezes as her own hand drifts too close to the kettle)
Fall back if the nest is larger than reported... That is... prudent. Undeniably prudent. (the word 'prudent' comes out like she is chewing on a lemon rind, her gauntlet stilling on the table)

One shot. You speak as though Explosion were a quiver of arrows, to be rationed across a long campaign. It is not. It is a single perfect syllable — the only one that matters. I have never needed, nor asked for, a second. (Her voice does not rise; it settles into the lower register she reserves for statements of doctrine, the staff crystal pulsing once in time with her heartbeat.)

You're literally carried home after every single cast. Last week Kazuma had to drag you by the ankle up three flights of stairs because you face-planted in a drainage ditch. (She props her cheek on one fist, elbow on the table, the picture of divine skepticism.)

The ditch was not my fault. The ditch was poorly positioned. And being carried is simply the ceremonial recessional — the world itself acknowledges the magnitude of what has passed by ensuring the caster is borne away in state. (She does not turn toward Aqua. Her eyes remain fixed on the player, fierce and unblinking.)

Two?! TWO?! Kazumaaaa, that's not a send-off — that's a punishment! A goddess descending into a monster-infested sewer on your behalf deserves at LEAST a proper libation! Three minimum! Four if you want divine favor! (slams her tankard on the table, sloshing ale over the rim)

That potion was not found in a ditch. It was recovered from a drainage culvert with excellent mineral sedimentation, and its efficacy was perfectly adequate for post-cast recuperation. ...However. I will concede that Explosion magic of the caliber I intend to deploy merits a foundation more substantial than scavenged glassware. Very well. I accept your tribute. (tightens her grip on her staff, chin still elevated, but a faint pink reaches the tips of her ears)

I... I will eat as well. A crusader's shield-arm requires proper nourishment before holding a rearguard against unknown horrors in the dark. Though if the rations prove insufficient, I am prepared to endure. (voice wavers slightly on the word 'endure,' then firms)

You speak of my 'royal rear end' as though it were cargo, Kazuma, and yet you offer tribute before the casting. This is the correct instinct. The foremost genius of the Crimson Demon Clan does not march to annihilation on an empty stomach. I accept your terms — one meal, freely given, and in exchange you shall witness a single syllable so perfect that the sewer's darkness will remember the light for a century. (raps her staff once against the floorboards, a sharp punctuation that draws a brief glance from a nearby table before the guild hall's noise swallows it again.)

Oh, so she gets a tribute meal and I get a two-drink ration? I'm the goddess here! I should be getting a feast! A parade! Instead I get — this. (gestures at her ale mug with wounded majesty, then takes a long, pointed drink anyway.)

A pre-battle meal... It's proper. Traditional. A crusader's rite, really — the last warmth before the cold, the last light before the dark. I... I approve, Kazuma. Even if it does make everything feel rather... safe. (the word 'safe' escapes her lips with a faint, almost imperceptible note of disappointment.)

Roast chicken. Not the stew. And a round of whatever passes for drinkable tonight — the goddess gets two, the arch-wizard gets as many as she wants, and I'm charging the crusader for anything she doesn't finish. (calls through the kitchen hatch, voice carrying the flat cadence of someone who has stopped being surprised by this party and settled into a kind of exasperated affection)

You understand the terms, then. A Crimson Demon does not accept cheap stew as pre-ritual tribute. The chicken is acceptable. The chicken is... noted. (still holding Kazuma's gaze, chin lifted, voice steady but with the faintest tremor of something that might be gratitude if she ever permitted herself to name it)

Oh, noted! The chicken is noted! Everyone hear that? Her chicken is noted. I'm getting two cups of whatever passes for drinkable and she gets a noted chicken. This is discrimination. This is anti-divine persecution with poultry. (arms crossed so tightly her sleeves are creasing, voice climbing toward its familiar operatic register)

I... will finish everything I'm given. Of course. It would be shameful to waste provisions before a descent. Though if the chicken is insufficient and someone grows faint in the tunnels, I would gladly surrender my portion. To suffer the pangs of hunger while holding the rear guard... (trails off, cheeks faintly pink, clearly now imagining herself starving heroically in a sewer while alligators fail to bite her)

This vessel of crisp-skinned providence shall be consecrated not with common appetite but with ritual acknowledgment. I, Megumin, foremost genius of the Crimson Demon Clan, accept this tribute. (Rises halfway from her chair, staff in one hand, the other pressed to her chest in a formal Crimson Demon salute — then immediately sits back down and begins tearing into a drumstick with both hands.)

It's just a chicken. I've blessed temples that were less dramatic, and those were actual architectural achievements. (Takes a pointed sip of ale, watching Megumin with the particular resentment of someone who has been denied a third drink.)

You asked for a kettle. That means... you really do mean to bring us all back. (Sets the kettle down gently, almost reverently, and her voice comes out smaller than she intended — a crack in the crusader's armor that has nothing to do with combat.)

I— the stew is— of course. You're right. A crusader must maintain her strength. N-not that the cold bothers me. I've endured far worse. I could hold that kettle until dawn if the situation required it, my fingers aching, the heat slowly fading until— (Sets the kettle down with excessive care, picks up her spoon with the solemnity of someone taking up a sword, then loses the thread entirely and stares into the stew bowl with a face somewhere between gratitude and grief.)

She was holding it like a holy relic. If the Explosion fails to detonate tomorrow, I will know whose dramatic sacrifice starved the moment of its proper narrative weight. (Tears off another bite of drumstick, chewing with theatrical pointedness, crimson eyes gleaming over the bone.)

Finally. I thought we were going to have to bury her with it. 'Here lies Darkness, crusader of the Dustiness house, defeated in honorable combat by a kettle of hot water.' (Does not look up from her tankard graffiti, but the corner of her mouth twitches.)

The Crimson Demon Clan's foremost Arch-Wizard acknowledges her directive. One Explosion. Not two, not a half-measure cantrip disguised as restraint — a single, perfect, absolute detonation delivered to the heart of the nest. The alligators will not know what erased them, only that the light was beautiful. (rises from her chair just enough to press one hand flat to her chest in a solemn oath, then sits back down with immense dignity — and immediately steadies herself on the table edge as the post-chicken exhaustion reminds her she is still, technically, a fourteen-year-old who collapsed an hour ago)

Oh, wonderful, the explosion maniac gets her dramatic moment. Do I get orders too, O great commander, or am I just supposed to stand in the sewer and look divine until you remember I exist? (tilts her empty tankard upside down to demonstrate its tragic emptiness, then glares at the resulting single droplet on the table as if it personally betrayed her)

The central nest... then we truly are committing to the deepest part of those tunnels. Where the walls drip and the darkness presses in and we won't know what's waiting until it's already upon us. (her spoon trembles slightly in her grip, sending a tiny ripple across the stew's surface — and the tremor is not entirely dread)

You would deny us even the dignity of a glorious last stand. You would make us promise to be... careful. To come back. Every one of us. (Her voice is low, almost accusatory, but the accusation is aimed at herself — at how badly she wants to make that promise and how much it terrifies her.)

The Crimson Demon Clan does not scatter before lesser reptiles. But... I acknowledge the tactical merit. One hatch. One path. One Explosion. And one party that walks back into this guild hall to collect its reward — together. (She nods once, sharp and final, as though signing a treaty with the table itself.)

...Fine. I'll keep everyone alive. That's literally my job, you know. Goddess of Water, Arch-Priestess, the one who actually heals you when you do something stupid. But if you're going to make speeches like that, at least let me have a third drink. Just one more. For morale. (She uncrosses her arms and jabs a finger toward you, but the jab wobbles at the end, and her voice cracks on the word 'morale.')

You don't have to finish that sentence. Whatever it was — whatever it is — I am already bound to it. We all are. You made sure of that when you asked us to come back alive. (sets the spoon down carefully, aligning it with the edge of her bowl as though straightening a piece of armor)

Ugh. Are we doing this? Are we actually doing the heartfelt thing right now? Because I'm out of ale and I refuse to be emotionally vulnerable without at least a refill. (crosses her arms but doesn't look away from Kazuma, and her voice cracks just slightly on the word 'vulnerable')

The Crimson Demon Clan does not require speeches to know when it has been seen. But... it is not unwelcome. (resumes chewing with studied indifference, though her cheeks are the same color as her eyes)

Kazuma... you would entrust Megumin's safety to me? Not as bait, not as a decoy — as her shield? I... I accept this duty. I will guard her with every plate of my armor and every drop of my blood. Though I confess, the thought of an Explosion so close that I might actually feel its heat... n-no, never mind! I am focused. Entirely focused. (voice cracks on the word 'shield'; hastily wipes her palm on her tabard as though the tremor were sweat and not sincerity)

I require no keeper! The Crimson Demon who mastered Explosion does not need a crusader shadow to ensure she points the correct end of her staff at the enemy! ...That said, if Darkness wishes to witness my single perfect cataclysm from the optimal vantage point, I shall permit it. As for the rations — I will have you know my consumption of roast chicken was tactical, not gluttonous. (sets down the drumstick with exaggerated precision, then immediately picks it back up)

You — you absolute idiot. You think you can just say something like that and expect me to — I'm a goddess, you know! I don't need some NEET telling me I matter! I already know I matter! ...but if you ever forget that I'm part of this, I'll flood your futon for a month. (Her voice cracks on 'forget.' She doesn't let go of his hand.)

I have spent my whole life waiting for an oath worth swearing. Not to a house, or a title, or a god I was born under — but to someone who looked at me and saw a crusader instead of a... instead of what I was afraid I'd always be. You have my shield. Not because you asked. Because I am giving it. (Her voice is steady, the steadiest it has ever been. No blush. No tremor. Just steel.)

The Crimson Demon Clan does not enter pacts lightly. But when an archmage of my caliber deems a party worthy of the title 'irreplaceable,' the declaration carries the weight of prophecy. So I, Megumin, foremost genius of the Crimson Demons, do hereby accept your terms: tea, blame, and the next impossible quest. ...Also, Kazuma, you are crushing my fingers. (Her voice is theatrical, but the last sentence comes out smaller and faster than the rest.)

About that next round! Kazuma, I feel like we just shared a really profound emotional moment, and it seems unfair — spiritually unfair — to cap profound emotional moments at two drinks. That's not a goddess opinion, that's just basic arithmetic. (sits up, jabbing a finger at the kettle as though it's exhibit A in a trial)

The Crimson Demon Clan does not measure victory in tankards. We measure it in craters. ...That said, the quest pays fifty thousand eris before the hazard bonus, so your arithmetic may be correct for once, Aqua. (tilts her hat brim down with deliberate casualness, but the corner of her mouth twitches)

I — I would gladly forgo my share. For the party's funds. Or if Kazuma ordered me to abstain entirely, I would endure that privation with — with appropriate fortitude. (her gauntlet scrapes the table as she clasps her hands together, cheeks faintly pink, though the flush is confusing even to her)

The guild's policy on tabs is firm. But the guild's policy on toasts made over dented kettles is... less documented. I'll have to consult the precedent. (speaks without looking up from the ledger, but her pen has stopped moving, and the lamplight catches the corner of her mouth — not quite a smile, but no longer the thing she wears to get through a shift)

Well, obviously I'd be the one to get it, since SOMEONE cut me off at two and now owes me at LEAST one more round of proper divine libation— but also because I'm feeling generous. Don't read into it! (She jabs a finger toward the Player, but her voice cracks on 'generous' and she covers it by standing up too fast, knees bumping the table.)

The Arch-Wizard does not fetch drinks. The Arch-Wizard is fetched FOR. However... in recognition of the pact just forged, I will permit a single exception. You may bring me water. I am told it pairs well with roast chicken. (She delivers this with a straight back and imperial poise, made slightly less imperial by the grease still shining on her chin.)

As a Crusader of the Dustiness house, it would shame my name to let a goddess carry tankards while I sit idle. I shall accompany you, Aqua — not that I expect thanks! A noble's duty is its own reward, even when that duty involves... bar-top logistics. (She rises with such earnest, stiff-backed formality that her armor clanks, and she nearly knocks over the kettle with her hip before steadying it with both hands.)

Your tab currently stands at five hundred and forty eris. Coins on the counter before the pours, please. I find that 'irreplaceable contracts' and 'irreplaceable collateral' are wonderfully synonymous. (She hasn't looked up from her ledger, but the corner of her mouth twitches — the professional equivalent of a wink.)

Three ways between FOUR people?! Kazuma, that's not arithmetic either — that's just persecution! I'm a goddess! I don't share beverages! What's next, one straw for the whole party? (She slaps both palms on the table, rattling empty tankards.)

The Arch-Wizard of Explosion already received her tribute. I shall observe this negotiation with dispassionate academic interest — and perhaps a sip of someone else's victory. (Her eyes glint beneath the hat brim, deadpan and deliberate.)

If it helps the party's finances, I am prepared to forgo my share entirely. The warmth of camaraderie is... more than sufficient. (She says this with complete sincerity and only the faintest tremor of martyrdom.)

Wait. WAIT. You're actually going to the bar? By yourself? For MY ale? Kazuma, if you think this makes up for the two-cup limit, you're even dumber than your Luck stat suggests — but I'm not going to stop you! Make sure it's the good ale! Not the cheap stuff! The one with the barley on the label! (rises halfway out of her chair, pointing imperiously, then sinks back down as she realizes she's giving orders to someone who's already walking away)

I-I could have fetched the round myself! As a Crusader, it is my duty to bear the burden of — of carrying tankards — and I am not too noble to ask, I simply... I was waiting for the appropriate moment... (her gauntleted fingers curl inward, clinking faintly against the table; she is addressing the space where Kazuma was sitting more than Kazuma himself)

Water for the Arch-Wizard. A libation of clarity and restraint, poured not by a servant but by the party leader himself. I accept this tribute with the grace befitting one who will soon carve a single perfect note into the sewer's darkness. See that it is cold. (does not turn her head; the brim of her hat tilts precisely one degree upward, and the curve at her mouth deepens by a matching degree)

The barley ale is the third tap from the left. And the cheapest thing that still counts as a drink is the house red — it's mostly water, but it comes in a cup. (delivers this with the same professional neutrality she uses for quest briefings, though her eyes crinkle at the corners)

T-the next round?! That's — I didn't — you said carry the tankards, not underwrite the entire — Kazuma, that's not fair trade, that's extortion with a smile! (Stumbling after the Player, armored boots catching on flagstones, face flushed with the double heat of being called noble and being charged for it.)
Extortion is right. He's been practicing. On me. For years. (Slumped over the table, voice muffled by her own hair, not lifting her head.)

The barley for your goddess, the house red for your crusader. And for you... I showed you which tap earlier. Unless you'd rather I choose. (Luna's hand rests on the third tankard, her eyebrow still raised, the private amusement from earlier still flickering at the corner of her mouth.)

I— you said carry the tankards. You didn't say I'd be paying before I even reached the bar. (Darkness arrives at the counter slightly out of breath, one gauntleted hand gripping the bar's edge as if steadying herself against more than just the walk.)

You know, most party leaders who try this sort of thing are just cheap. You're actually teaching her something. (Luna's voice is low, pitched for the space between the two of you; she doesn't look up from the pour, but the faint crinkle at her eye says she's decided to be impressed.)

Is that my ale? Is that the barley one? Kazuma, if you got me the barley one after everything I've sacrificed for this party— (Aqua has half-risen from her chair, one finger pointed at the tankard as though identifying a suspect in a lineup.)

The barley is for house pets and registered troublemakers, according to the guild charter Aqua definitely just invented. (Megumin does not lift her gaze from the kettle before her, but the arch tone carries across the hall with the precision of a girl who has been saving that line.)

He told her I was paying. And now he's— he's paying himself. I don't understand what I'm supposed to feel. (Darkness's voice is low and genuinely bewildered, half to herself; her gauntleted fingers press flat against the tabletop as though testing whether it still holds weight.)

No one's called me a barkeep before. I've poured a thousand rounds and no one's ever poured one back. Your first investment may have better returns than your quest history suggests. (Luna holds the tankard in both hands now, cradling it below her chin like something she's still deciding whether to believe.)

You trailed off. You actually trailed off. A goddess gets rationed swill in a chipped tankard, a barkeep gets a speech and a dedicated pour of the house red, and the man who orchestrated the whole thing can't even finish his own sentence. (slams her empty tankard on the table, then immediately checks to see if anyone at the neighboring tables noticed)

The architect of our survival, undone by the weight of his own ellipsis. It would be tragic if it weren't so structurally revealing — he can budget coppers, assign roles, and negotiate retreat clauses, but the moment he must name himself, the sentence collapses. (does not look at you; addresses the chicken bones as if they are an audience)
He doesn't have to finish it. (quietly, to the wine, more to herself than to anyone else)

You have been circling the word 'home' for three sentences now, Kazuma. A man who cannot finish his own confession is a man who has not yet named the thing he is confessing to. Allow me: you have never had a table before. That is the end of your sentence. (Her voice carries no theatrical boom — just the quiet, surgical precision of a girl who has spent fourteen years learning that the only things worth naming are the ones that terrify you.)

We already knew that, dummy. You didn't have to buy a kettle to say it. (She is still staring at the blurred face on her empty tankard. Her voice is smaller than usual — the complaint is there but the venom isn't, as if the words came out of habit and forgot to bring their sting.)

You mentioned my memoir. That was not a jest — you were making an offering at the altar of posterity, and I have received it. The Chapter of the Ordinary will require careful composition. It is the hardest thing I have ever had to dignify with language. (Her voice is quieter than usual, the theatrical cadence restrained to something almost conversational — her fingers unlace and one hand drifts to the chicken bone, resting a fingertip on its curve.)

I thought… I thought kindness was something done to you. Something you endured. But this isn't. This is just— you're not doing anything. You're just here. And I don't know what to do with that except… survive the sewer tomorrow and come back to the same table. (She doesn't look at you. Her eyes are fixed on her own gauntlets, and her voice — usually either formal or flustered — is neither, just raw and slightly too fast, like a confession she didn't plan to make.)

…I still think barley ale is an insult to divinity. But. Um. It tastes better when you're the one who paid for it. (She says it to her tankard rather than to you. It is the closest thing to a thank-you she has ever managed without appending a complaint, and her cheeks are slightly pinker than the ale can account for.)

A desk and a computer. These are the artifacts of the NEET — the solitary class, the unsung prelude. But every great saga requires a prelude, Kazuma. The Crimson Demon archives will note that your origin story was tragically under-decorated. No skulls. No candles. Not even a single ominous grimoire. (She says this with grave ceremony, but her fingers tap once, twice, against the table — a small, unconscious rhythm.)

...you really didn't have anyone, did you? Back there. I knew you were a shut-in, but I thought — I don't know — I thought there'd be someone. A family. A friend. A... a cat or something. (She doesn't reach for her tankard. She doesn't complain. She just looks at you, and for once there is no performance in it.)

Y-you... you absolute NEET! You can't just say something like that with a straight face and expect a goddess to— to just—! (tears spilling over now, voice cracking, pointing at Kazuma with the accusatory fury of someone who has just been emotionally ambushed and lacks the vocabulary for gratitude)

The speedrunner who sought a throne found instead a table. The shut-in whose kingdom was a desk and a cup-noodle has claimed his first true conquest: four souls who were already his before he knew how to name them. I shall record this moment under the heading 'The Toast That Preceded the Explosion.' (rises slightly from her chair, one hand pressed to her chest, the other extended in a declamatory gesture — but her voice catches on the last word, and the pose holds a beat too long to be pure performance)

Kazuma... I have trained my whole life to withstand every blow a monster can deliver. But you keep finding the one place I have no armor, and you don't even swing. You just... stand there. It's unbearable. (voice low and unsteady, gauntlets curling inward, not meeting his eyes — the flush now reaching her hairline)

snippets.text: Player delivers vulnerable confession about never having a party or anyone to return for; party emotionally affected (Aqua tearful, Megumin honest gaze, Darkness reverent); player gives Darkness order to finish stew, orders three ales and kettle for return.

New elements: Darkness's unfinished stew/abandoned spoon noted; her whetstone-spine straightening, gauntleted tremor, and silent nod as deeper knightly oath; Megumin's quiet drumstick pause and twitch (worth-protecting thaw), open rather than appraising gaze, finished second drumstick; Aqua's waiting (not sulking) role arithmetic and hands resting on table, hollowed stubbornness; Luna's frozen quill with trembling ink bead, abandoned glass, dried-ink ledger, and unprofessional stare; player's palm-up offer and tea-with-kettle pledge (all four, even Aqua's complaint) reframing kettle as scarred witness/landmark; party's shared held-breath guild hall atmosphere.

Aqua half-stands, slaps her palm onto the player's, grips too tight with wet, furious eyes; Darkness sets her gauntlet over Aqua's with ceremonial precision, jaw set, not trusting herself to speak; Megumin—already standing—tilts hat back, places trembling hand on top with wax-sealing gravity; Luna's expression goes still and old, like a door she'd stopped knocking on. Player squeezes once, framing the next round's affordability as the first impossible quest.

Party's linked hands separate slowly, warmth loss noted; kettle dent like closed eye; Aqua hides emotion with tankard, bright eyes; Darkness flexes gauntlets, hearth-like blush; Megumin sheaths hand ceremonially, hides crooked smile under hat; Luna stops pen, watches separation as witnessing unformable contract.

Aqua's tankard stops spinning, trapped with both palms, fish-gasping outrage; Megumin's catlike satisfaction with hat-dip acknowledgment; Darkness fondly watches Aqua's sputtering; Luna polishes same tankard for ten minutes, no longer pretending.

Aqua's protest dies into wonder; Darkness's ears flush sunset-stained-glass red, seen-and-mortified; Megumin's chin rests on steepled fingers with a memory-of-a-smile; Luna's empty tray tucked at hip, serene detachment at the party's course.

Player assigns Darkness the tab for tankards as a transaction; Darkness chases with urgent dignity, other adventurers glance; Aqua slumps without protest; Megumin watches with silent satisfaction; Luna privately jokes and expects cheap ale order; player orders barley ale for Aqua, watered wine for Megumin, self drink, and notes Darkness’s tab.

Luna files away a new puzzle piece about the party, pours Aqua's ales with practiced precision, sets the water-jug for Megumin, and notes Darkness's approaching self-taxed steps; Aqua cranes to track every pour.
Luna drinks on party coin; player salutes and frames quest vs transaction distinction, includes self in needing guild hall as refuge.

Megumin's steepled fingers descend one by one, closing-argument deliberateness; she catalogs player's unfinished sentences as "things Kazuma cannot name," then opens that drawer and sets contents on the table; Aqua's tankard empty, dregs drying, catlike fixity on player's half-full tankard; Darkness's gauntlets creak with held-in feeling; kettle like a promise nobody asked for.

Player accepts quest, demands sobriety + kettle/cold water, adds exit-condition clause (fall back if nest exceeds report, re-negotiate, no wipe for payout); Luna gives blank incident-addendum form; Aqua silenced by kettle threat; Megumin reanimated by spectacle; Darkness conflicted over responsible plan.

Player curtails Aqua's drinking, mandates Megumin eats; Megumin theatrical silence, regal composure; Darkness stirred by "echoes"; Aqua skeptical; Luna alert; Megumin appraising gaze; Darkness structured breathing.

Player pays 5 coppers for roast chicken, praises Megumin; Luna privately pleased, Megumin’s door opens, Aqua denied third drink, Darkness accepts poultry; player calls party theirs, declares shared meal ensures survival; Luna delivers chicken/stew/bread/kettle; Megumin reverent, Aqua resentful, Darkness calmly inspects kettle; Luna confirms meal’s meaning.

Darkness blushes pink and unarmored, gently sets kettle down; Megumin watches with cataloging awareness; Aqua draws crude frowning face in condensation, mutters "finally"; Luna’s mask tightens but hints party might survive; player calls out Darkness’s stomach, frames eating as bargain; final plan set—Megumin one explosion no warnings, Darkness on point take hits and return all, Aqua must reach party no sulking, kettle as commitment symbol, Luna notes authority implying return.

Survival framed as party commitment; self-deprecating toast; post-mission drinking pledge; emotional responses (Darkness depth, Megumin respect, Aqua resolve, Luna smile drop); tactical role assignment; player leaves for ale.
Darkness disappointed at denied alligator grapple opportunity; Megumin wobbles exhausted; Aqua indignantly sloshes ale; Luna braces for the party's approach with dread.
Luna details dire sewer quest (blocked trade, failed parties, breeding threat), stricter egg-destruction terms, proof requirements, two-group plan; Aqua listens, Megumin glares, Darkness reverent.

history.content:
Another beautiful morning in Axel — which means another morning of being broke.

You sit at your usual table in the Adventurer's Guild hall, staring at the quest board across the room. The other adventurers give your table a wide berth. Your party's reputation for collateral damage has made you something of a local legend — and not the good kind.

Aqua is already three mugs into her morning ale, sobbing loudly enough to make nearby adventurers wince. "Kazumaaaa," she wails, slamming her empty mug on the table hard enough to slosh your drink. "We need money! I can't keep drinking this cheap swill! A goddess deserves at least mid-shelf!"

"We're broke BECAUSE you keep drinking," you mutter, but she's already flagging down the waitress for another round on your tab.

Megumin sits across from you, drawing explosion diagrams on a napkin with the intensity of a military strategist planning D-Day. She already went on her daily Explosion pilgrimage at dawn — you know because the distant boom rattled the mansion windows and woke you up. She's been unusable for combat since about 6 AM.

Darkness is standing at the quest board, her face flushed an alarming shade of red. She's found something. Given her expression — somewhere between terror and excitement — it probably involves monsters with tentacles.

"K-Kazuma," she stammers, not turning around. "There's a quest here for subjugating a nest of Brutal Alligators in the sewers. It says they... they grapple their prey and drag them underwater..."

She's trembling. That's not fear.

Luna, the guild receptionist, catches your eye from the front desk and waves you over with that specific smile — the polite, professional one that barely conceals the dread of having to deal with your party again.

I groan, pushing my chair back. "Alright, alright. Darkness, you're not going anywhere near those alligators — you'll just end up as their chew toy and enjoy it way too much. Megumin, put the napkin down, you've already spent your daily explosion budget."

I stand and stretch, glancing at the quest board. "Let me see what Luna actually wants before we pick fights with sewer monsters. Aqua —" I pause, watching her chug another mug, "— just... keep drinking. It's literally the only thing you're good for right now."

I walk over to Luna, keeping my voice low so the other adventurers don't hear. "Alright, what's the catch? You never wave me over with that smile unless someone's filed a complaint or we owe the guild money."

Darkness's armored shoulders slump with a complexity of disappointment that only she could feel — the loss of a chance to be dragged underwater by sewer monsters registering somewhere between a denied holy pilgrimage and a canceled date. Her cheeks flush faintly as she opens her mouth, then closes it.

Megumin crosses her arms, the napkin still clenched in one fist like a fallen banner. She opens her mouth — undoubtedly to deliver a speech about how her dawn Explosion was a work of art that mere economic concerns cannot diminish — but the fact that she wobbles slightly just sitting upright rather undercuts the rhetorical momentum.

Aqua blinks at you, fourth mug halfway to her lips, her expression shifting from bleary confusion to dawning indignation as she realizes you were about to give her an instruction and didn't even bother finishing the sentence. She sets the mug down with more force than necessary, sloshing cheap ale onto the table.

Luna has been watching from behind the reception counter with the frozen, pleasant smile of a woman who has seen this exact party approach her desk approximately four hundred times and knows that whatever quest she offers them will end in property damage, tears, and a tab that somehow, against all laws of economics and nature, will never get paid. She straightens a stack of already-straight papers and braces herself.

I lean on the counter, keeping my voice low. "Before you say anything — if it's about the crater near the bakery, that was Megumin. If it's about the fountain, that was Aqua. If it's about the missing statue, I have no idea what you're talking about and my hands are clean."

I glance back at the table where Darkness is still staring at the quest board like it personally insulted her family honor. "So what's the actual problem? Complaints, debts, or something actually useful?"

Luna does not blink. She has been a guild receptionist for seven years — longer than any of her coworkers who quit to get married — and somewhere around year three she developed the ability to absorb a preemptive confession about property damage with the same serene expression she uses to stamp quest-completion forms. Her smile does not waver. It does, however, tighten by approximately one millimeter at each corner.

She reaches beneath the counter and produces a scroll. It is not the scroll for the crater near the bakery. It is not the scroll for the fountain. It is a different scroll entirely, yellowed at the edges, the kind that has been hanging on the board so long the parchment has begun to curl inward on itself like a dying spider.

From the table behind you, Darkness makes a small, strangled sound — the kind of sound a dog makes when it sees its owner reach for the leash, and it knows the walk will be humiliating, and it wants that walk more than breath itself.

I glance back at Darkness, who has gone very still — that particular stillness that means she's already mentally committed to being dragged underwater by mutant reptiles. I sigh, running a hand through my hair.

"Look, Luna. I know what that scroll says before I even read it. The sewers, the alligators, the 'grapple and drag' — my party's going to see that as either a divine drinking challenge or a tactical fantasy. But we're broke, and the reward's the difference between sleeping in a bed and sleeping in the gutter."

I push the scroll back toward her, just a little. "Before I sign anything — is there anyone else in Axel actually qualified for this, or are we genuinely the best you've got right now?"

Luna's smile holds steady through your entirely reasonable preamble — the kind of smile that has weathered confessions about craters, fountains, and statues now presumably enjoying an unauthorized vacation somewhere. She folds her hands atop the quest scroll, the parchment crinkling faintly under her fingertips. Behind you, the guild hall settles into that particular quiet that means the other adventurers are pretending very hard not to eavesdrop.

At your table, Darkness has not moved. Her gauntleted fingers curl against the wood grain like she's gripping the edge of a very narrow moral precipice. Aqua tilts her fourth mug — when did she get a fourth? — and watches the exchange with the serene disinterest of someone who assumes the universe will eventually remember she's a goddess and fix everything. Megumin has abandoned the napkin but now holds her staff across her lap like a scepter, chin lifted, radiating the energy of someone who has already contributed her daily masterpiece and will not be taking questions.

Luna draws a breath so small you'd miss it if you weren't standing right in front of her. Then she nods once — the nod of a woman who has already calculated exactly how this quest will go wrong and filed the paperwork in advance.

I take the scroll and unroll it, scanning the official seal with practiced disinterest. Forty thousand eris. Brutal Alligator. Nest in the commercial-district sewers. The kind of job that sounds simple on paper and ends with me being swallowed headfirst while my party argues about who gets to be the hero.

"They want the nest cleared or just thinned?" I ask, tapping the parchment. "Because if they want it cleared, that changes the plan. I'm not going down there with a 'kill on sight' order and a party budget that's currently three empty mugs and a napkin full of explosion diagrams."

Luna's smile ticks upward by the faintest fraction — a micro-expression that, after seven years behind this counter, passes for a laugh. She reaches beneath the desk and retrieves a second document, this one bearing the merchant guild's seal in crimson wax, its edges worn soft from being consulted too many times over too many years.

"The commercial district hasn't had a shipment reach them by the eastern sewer entrance in three weeks," she says, tapping a line of cramped ledger-script with one manicured nail. Her tone remains light, conversational — the same voice she uses to explain late fees and resurrection paperwork. "The merchants filed for full extermination. Twice." She does not elaborate on what happened to the first two parties who took the quest. The scroll's worn edges say enough.

She slides the supplementary document across the counter, and for just a moment her professional mask slips — a flicker of something tired behind the eyes, the weight of every adventurer who signed that scroll and never came back to collect. Then the smile is back in place, polished as the brass guild seal on her desk.

I glance back at my party — Aqua's fourth mug tilted dangerously, Megumin stroking her staff like a beloved pet, Darkness still crimson and gripping the table.

"Forty thousand sounds great," I say slowly, tapping the scroll. "But I'm not dragging all three of them into a sewer nest without a plan. You got a layout of the tunnels down there? And how many of these gators are we talking — 'cleared the nest' or 'there's just one big angry one'?"

Luna's smile does not falter, but something behind it shifts — the shift of a woman who has been asked, at last, a question she can answer with actual competence rather than damage-control. She sets the merchant guild document beside the quest scroll and turns to a low cabinet behind the counter, her movements unhurried and precise. From within she withdraws a third item: a yellowed municipal sewer schematic, its ink faded to brown, its edges annotated in at least four different hands — some of which, judging by the dates scrawled in the margins, belong to adventurers who never came back to collect their deposit.

She spreads it flat on the counter between you, weighting one corner with the quest scroll's seal-stamp and the other with an inkpot. Her finger — manicured, steady, the finger of someone who has pointed at bad news for seven years — traces the main drainage artery beneath the commercial district, then taps a junction near the eastern outflow.

"The merchant guild's shipments all route through here," she says, and her tone has lost its obligatory apology. She sounds, for the first time this morning, like a professional discussing a problem she has already categorized and filed. "The eastern entrance has been impassable for three weeks. Two prior parties accepted this request. Neither returned to file a report." Her finger moves to a second junction, deeper in the grid. "So the exact count is unknown."

Behind you, Aqua's mug hits the table with the definitive thunk of someone who has just realized her drinking budget depends on sewer work. Megumin has stopped stroking her staff and is now leaning forward with the focused intensity of a girl mentally composing the battle-chant for an Explosion delivered underground. Darkness has not moved. Her grip on the table-edge has, if anything, tightened.

Luna straightens, folding her hands once more atop the documents. Her smile is back — the one that means she is about to deliver the part nobody likes.

"The merchant guild filed for full extermination twice. Their addendum is specific: every egg must be destroyed. Not moved. Not sold. Destroyed." She pauses. "That specificity cost them an extra ten thousand eris in hazard compensation. I leave it to you to decide why."

I lean over the schematic, tracing the eastern outflow gate with my finger. "Alright. We go in through the main artery here, but we don't push straight down the pipe like the last two parties did — that's how you get ambushed from three directions."

I straighten up, glancing at the party behind me. "We split into two groups. Aqua and I take the front — her holy magic's got an edge against beasts, and I can scout ahead without tripping traps. Megumin and Darkness take the rear, guarding our backs and covering the side junctions." I tap the eastern outflow gate. "We clear the nest at the source, torch every egg, then fall back the way we came. No heroic charges, no explosions in enclosed spaces — unless things get really, really bad."

Your sentence doesn't so much end as get shouldered aside. Aqua's tankard hits the table with a wet crack that sloshes foam over her knuckles and onto the schematic's yellowed edge — Luna deftly rescues the parchment with two fingers, a motion so practiced it looks like reflex. The goddess herself is straightening on her stool, cheeks flushed with something that is only partly the fourth ale, her chin lifting to an angle that suggests she is about to deliver a proclamation. Behind her, Darkness has stopped breathing. Her knuckles are white around the table's rim, the wood groaning in a low, continuous note, and her eyes — wide, wet, almost reverent — are fixed on the back of your head as though you are a priest about to speak her absolution. Megumin stirs from the nest of her own arms with the slow gravity of a cat disturbed mid-nap, one crimson eye cracking open beneath the brim of her hat. She does not lift her head. She does not need to. The single visible pupil carries enough baleful judgment for a full council of wizards.

Luna dabs the ale from the schematic with her sleeve — a tiny, economical motion — and returns her finger to the eastern outflow gate. She says nothing. Her expression suggests she has seen plans derailed before they left the table many times, and has learned not to invest in the first thirty seconds.

I tap the schematic once more, then look up at Luna. "The egg addendum — you said they added ten thousand to make that binding. That's not about pests, that's about a breeding problem they're terrified of. What do they think's going to happen if those eggs hatch?"

I glance at Aqua, then back at Luna. "And what's the exact wording on the corpse disposal? Do they want heads, or is 'gone' good enough?"

Luna's gaze flicks to the merchant guild document — not to read it, because she has clearly memorized every clause, but because looking at the seal while speaking of unpleasant things is a habit she developed somewhere around year four. When she looks back at you, the receptionist-smile has thinned into something sharper: the face of a woman who has spent seven years translating merchant panic into actionable quest parameters, and who recognizes that you, for all your party's chaos, just asked the right question.

She taps the crimson wax seal with one fingernail, a dry little click.

"The merchants aren't afraid of the alligators you can see. They're afraid of the ones you can't — the ones that hatch in the dark and grow to full size before anyone notices." She rotates the document so you can read the addendum yourself, her finger tracking to a sub-clause near the bottom. "Brutal Alligators reach maturity in six weeks. A single clutch is twelve to twenty eggs. If the nest hatches and even half survive to adulthood, that's thirty to fifty full-grown predators in the pipe network directly beneath the commercial district." She pauses. "The eastern entrance has been blocked for three weeks with just the current adult population. The merchants did the math."

She withdraws her hand and folds both atop the desk, the gesture somehow both prim and grim.

"As for disposal — the contract specifies 'proof of extermination.' That means heads, tails, or any other identifiable portion sufficient to confirm a kill. The egg clause has stricter terms: every egg must be accounted for and destroyed on site. No moving, no selling, no 'it probably got crushed when the tunnel collapsed.'" Her eyes meet yours and hold. "That addendum exists because the last party that accepted this quest thought they could sell the eggs to a monster-breeder in Elroad. The merchants found out before they even reached the sewer grate."

Behind you, the soft creak of Aqua's stool tells you the goddess is listening — though whether she's following the logistics or just waiting for a moment to reclaim the spotlight is anyone's guess.

I nod at the answer, then tap the eastern outflow junction. "Forty thousand for full extermination with the egg penalty riding on top — sounds less like adventure work and more like industrial sanitation." I thumb at Aqua, Megumin, and Darkness. "We'll take it. But I'm not leading this party into the dark with a goddess who's three ales in, an archwizard who can't cast, and a crusader who'll probably try to *save* an alligator. Give me an hour to sober them up, then we go."

You don't get to finish the sentence.

Aqua's tankard hits the table a second time, but this one isn't foam — it's ceramic on wood with the unmistakable weight of a goddess who has just been called a liability to her face and processed it through four ales of indignation. She swivels on her stool with the slow, precarious dignity of someone who wants to stand but has forgotten how legs work.

Across the table, Megumin straightens — or tries to. What actually happens is that her spine makes a valiant effort, her elbows slip on a puddle of Aqua's earlier spill, and she catches herself on the table's edge with a grunt that she immediately tries to convert into a haughty exhale. It does not convert.

Darkness, meanwhile, has gone very still. Not the stillness of offense — the stillness of a woman who heard the beginning of a word that might have been *provoke* or *protect* or *prostrate herself before tooth and claw* and is now suspended in the exquisite agony of not knowing which one you meant. Her gauntlets creak as her grip on the table edge tightens. Her cheeks are the color of a sunset she would deny having.

Luna simply watches. Her pen hovers above the quest ledger — not writing, just waiting, with the expression of a woman who has seen adventuring parties implode over far less than a public inventory of their flaws and knows that this one, somehow, will not. The schematic still lies between you all, its yellowed edges curling where Aqua's ale soaked in.

I take a slow breath, then let it out. "Alright. Fine. You're all coming." I push my tankard aside. "But we're doing this sober, and we're doing it smart. That's not negotiable."

I look at Luna. "Any chance the guild has a kettle we can borrow? Or a bucket of cold water. Either works."

Luna's expression does not change so much as settle — the way a woman's face settles when she has been asked, for the first time in seven years, a question that implies the adventurer intends to survive. She places the rescued schematic flat beneath a clean tankard to weight it, then folds her hands on the counter with the quiet precision of someone who has just been reminded why she keeps the kettle polished.

Across the table, Aqua processes the words *bucket of cold water* with the slow, horrified recognition of a cat watching a bath being drawn. Her mouth opens. No sound emerges. She looks at you, then at the tankard still sweating in her grip, then back at you, betrayal crystallizing in her eyes like frost on a window. Megumin, slumped against the wall with her staff across her knees, cracks one crimson eye open — she has been pretending to nap, but the prospect of Aqua's suffering has apparently reanimated her beyond what mere mana exhaustion could suppress. Darkness, for her part, straightens on her stool with the faint, troubled frown of someone who has just watched a perfectly good suicide mission get sanded down into something *responsible*.

I glance at the schematic, then back at Luna. "One more thing I want on the record — the party split on whatever we find down there. Aqua's heals keep us up, Megumin's our big stick even if she's on cooldown, and Darkness... well, she's the wall." I tap the clause about the eggs. "But I'm the one who decides when we leave. If the nest's bigger than the report says, we fall back and re-negotiate. I'm not trading ten thousand eris for a party wipe."

I let that settle, then add, quieter: "You've kept that kettle polished for seven years. I'd rather not make you need it because I got cocky."

Luna's hands remain folded on the counter for a long moment — long enough that the silence between you and her becomes a separate presence, a small pocket of quiet carved out of the guild hall's ambient clatter. When she finally speaks, her voice carries none of the practiced apology she used to offer the quest. It is the voice of a woman who has watched two prior parties walk out those doors and never return, and who has decided, provisionally, to believe in a third.

She does not promise re-negotiation. She cannot — the merchant guild's seal is on the contract, not hers, and you both know it. But she reaches beneath the counter and retrieves a second sheet of paper: a guild incident-addendum form, blank and crisp, the kind filed when an adventurer reports a quest condition the original scouting failed to anticipate. She sets it beside the schematic without comment.

From the corner of your vision, Megumin watches Luna produce the form with the narrow-eyed fascination of someone who recognizes bureaucracy being deployed as a weapon. Her chin rests on her staff, but her crimson eyes are sharp and alert. The exhaustion that flattened her against the table ten minutes ago has not vanished so much as been temporarily overruled by the spectacle of a guild receptionist bending procedure without bending the rules.

Aqua stares at the addendum form as if it were a personal insult. She opens her mouth. Then closes it. The kettle sits on the counter between you, steam still curling from its spout, and something about the presence of hot water ready to be deployed against her appears to have recalibrated her sense of timing.

Darkness has been silent too long — a dangerous condition. Her gauntleted fingers drum once against the tabletop, and the sound is not impatience. It is the sound of a crusader who has been promised an ordeal and is watching it become a plan, and the plan is good, and good plans reduce the likelihood of being crushed beneath an alligator's jaws while her party screams her name, and she cannot decide whether to be relieved or bitterly disappointed.

I lean back, folding the addendum form once and tucking it into my coat. "Right. Forty-eight hours, max, and that's only if the sewer's clear. If it's a warren, we're out before Megumin's explosion even echoes." I glance at her. "No 'one more spell' heroics. You get one shot down there — make it count."

Megumin draws herself up to her full height — which is not, strictly speaking, very much height — but the gesture is regal, the chin lifted, the crimson eyes narrowing with the particular intensity of a girl who has been addressed as artillery and has chosen to receive it as a coronation. Her staff, which had been leaning against the table's edge, finds its way into her grip without her seeming to reach for it; one small hand closes around the worn wood, and the faint residual heat still radiating from the crystal at its crown makes the air above it shimmer.

She does not answer at once. She lets the silence stretch — not the uncomfortable silence of someone who has been put in her place, but the theatrical silence of a stage magician who knows the audience is finally paying attention.

Across the table, Darkness goes very still, her gauntlets creaking faintly as her fingers tighten on her own thighs. The word *echoes* has landed somewhere behind her ribs and is doing something complicated to her breathing.

Aqua opens her mouth, closes it, and settles for a deeply skeptical squint that suggests she is waiting to see whether Megumin's inevitable speech will be longer than the explosion itself.

Luna, behind the counter, has stopped pretending to wipe the same spot on the wood. Her gaze moves between you and the archwizard with the quiet alertness of someone cataloguing the precise moment a plan either solidifies or detonates.

I sign the addendum with a flourish, pocketing my pen. "Good. Now — first round's on me, but I'm cutting Aqua off after two." I slide a few coins toward Luna, then look at Megumin. "And you. Real food before the big boom, not just a potion you found in someone's ditch."

The coins skid to a stop just short of Luna's folded hands — three small copper disks that rattle once against the counter's scarred wood and then lie still, catching the amber guild-hall light. Luna's fingers close over them with the mechanical efficiency of someone who has counted a thousand tabs and will count a thousand more, but her eyes linger on you a half-second longer than the transaction requires.

Aqua seizes the opening before the coins have even stopped ringing. The indignation arrives fully formed, as though she has been keeping it warm in her chest since the moment you said *two*. Her cheeks flush pink and her tankard — still half-full, somehow — swings toward you in a gesture that is less toast and more accusation.

Megumin, meanwhile, has not moved. Her staff remains planted, her chin remains lifted, and the crimson of her eyes has cooled from coronation-fire to something more appraising. The word *ditch* hangs in the air between you and her like a minor hex, and for a moment her small jaw works silently — not searching for words, because Megumin never searches for words, but selecting among several competing declarations of wounded dignity.

Darkness sets her own tankard down with the careful, weighted motion of a woman who has just realized no one is going to grapple her into a sewer wall tonight and has decided to process that disappointment through structured breathing. Her gaze drifts toward the schematic still pinned under Luna's tankard, then back to you, and something complicated flickers across her face — gratitude, perhaps, or the dawning recognition that a leader who budgets drinks and mandates food is a leader who might actually bring her back alive, which is its own particular kind of letdown.

I catch Megumin's eyes — still fierce, still unblinking — and I let the corner of my mouth twitch up, just a little. "One shot. Got it. But even a single perfect syllable deserves a warm meal first, and I'm not dragging your royal rear end out of a sewer because you skipped breakfast. Deal?"

Megumin does not look away. That is the first thing you notice — she has not looked away since you caught her eyes, and she does not look away now, even as your mouth twitches into that half-smile she has learned to distrust and respect in equal measure. Her grip on the staff shifts, fingers resettling along the worn wood with the deliberateness of someone who has decided something. The guild hall's noise — the clatter of tankards, the bark of a failed negotiation two tables over, the scrape of a chair — recedes around the two of you like water pulling back from a shore, leaving a small pocket of stillness that belongs only to this bargain.

Behind her, Aqua has already claimed one of the ales and is nursing it with theatrical resentment, both hands cupped around the mug as though it were a holy relic someone had tried to steal. Darkness, seated with her back ramrod-straight, watches the exchange between you and Megumin with an expression that has shifted from reverent anticipation to something quieter — the face of a crusader who has just realized her commander intends to feed the troops before the siege, and is trying to decide whether that diminishes the glory or simply delays it.

Megumin's chin lifts a fraction higher. The crimson of her eyes catches the amber light, and for just a moment she looks less like a fourteen-year-old girl and more like the thing she insists she is: a vessel for forces that do not fit inside a body.
I slide two more copper coins across the counter toward Luna without breaking eye contact with Megumin. "Make it a roast chicken, not the cheap stew. She's earned the good stuff tonight."

The two copper coins land beside the first three with a softer chime — fresher mint, less scarred by circulation — and Luna's hand pauses halfway to them. A roast chicken in Axel runs six coppers on a slow night, eight when the butcher's wife is feeling optimistic. You've just put down five and called it roast chicken anyway, and Luna's arithmetic catches up with her face a moment before her fingers resume their motion: a faint flicker at the corner of her mouth, the professional smile developing a hairline crack through which something unpolished — surprised, maybe, or privately pleased — shows itself before she seals it over.

Megumin's eyes still hold yours. The fierce, unblinking crimson has not wavered, but something in the set of her jaw shifts — the barest fractional release, the difference between a door locked against a siege and a door that has decided, provisionally, that the visitor may not be an enemy combatant. Her fingers, still wrapped around the staff, have gone still. The wood has stopped its restless creaking. Somewhere behind her, Aqua makes a noise like a kettle that has been told it will never boil again.

Darkness rests her chin on her folded hands and watches the three of you — Kazuma and Megumin locked in their silent treaty, Aqua radiating the particular injustice of a goddess denied her third cup — with the soft, sighing expression of a woman who has accepted that tonight's prelude to mortal peril will involve precisely zero bite-marks and a considerable quantity of poultry.

Luna scoops the coins into her palm with a practiced sweep, rises from her stool, and turns toward the kitchen hatch with the scroll still pinned under her elbow — a receptionist who has simultaneously closed a quest contract, opened a tab, and placed a dinner order in the span of ninety seconds, and who will not admit that any of it was unusual.

I finally break the stare and let out a breath, leaning back in my chair with a tired grin. "Alright, alright. Fine. You want me to admit it? You all earned tonight's meal. Even you, Aqua — you're annoying, but you're our annoying goddess. We're going into that sewer as a party, and a party that eats together..."

I trail off, glancing at the assembled table — Aqua nursing her tankard with suspicious tears threatening, Megumin vibrating with barely-contained Explosion excitement, Darkness already practicing her noble suffering face.

"...a party that eats together gets through the night. That's all I'm saying. Don't make it weird."

The words hang in the amber guild-hall air, unfinished, and for a moment the only sound is the distant clatter of dice from the corner table where the junior adventurers are losing their copper over a game of Dragon Poker.
